newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SHUT THE DOOR ON PARMA'S HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SHUT THE DOOR ON PARMA'S HOPES.

text.p: Juventus swamped Roma 3-0 on Saturday to go eight points clear of nearest rivals Parma at the top of Italy's serie A thanks to two first half goals from stand-in striker Christian Vieri.

But second-placed Parma, more realistically chasing a place in the European Cup as runners-up, can cut the gap to five points if they beat third placed Inter Milan later in a key match likely to end one team's title hopes.

Vieri, the main target man of a below-strength Juventus, scored in the 28th and 44th minutes to dismiss any notion that the absence of injured striker Alessandro del Piero and suspended Croat Alen Boksic had weakened the team.

The first goal was a low, rasping shot past surprised goalkeeper Giovanni Cervone after Nicola Amoruso fed the ball through. The second was worthy of the boy wonder Del Piero himself, a neat diagonal loop into the net.
Amoruso made it 3-0 in the 85th when Michele Padovano, brought on as a second half substitute, missed a sitting chance but made amends by setting up his team mate.

Juventus, whose match was brought forward from the usual Sunday slot to allow more time to prepare for Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final second leg against Norway's Rosenborg, now have 48 points after 24 matches.
Vieri's goals will have given the Rosenborg scouts little encouragement since he was also the scorer of a lightning equaliser in the 1-1 first leg draw in Norway.
Parma have 40 points and Inter, who drew 0-0 with Juventus at the San Siro last weekend, are on 38.
Juventus fans have no doubts that they will be following their team into the Champions' League next season and Saturday's result at the Stadio delle Alpi reinforced that.
But the venue also added to a sense of unease, with fans unsure where they will be watching Juventus when Italian soccer's "Old Lady" celebrates her 100th anniversary this year.
The club is locked in a dispute with the city authorities over rents on the cavernous delle Alpi stadium.

Newspapers have reported that the club's officials want to stay in Turin but have already made contingency plans by approaching Reggiana to play league matches at their Reggio Emilia ground and cup matches at Milan's San Siro.
A showdown is forecast for the coming week.

Ironically, while the procession to a record 24th league "scudetto" (title shield) continues at a stately pace, the next few days could have more of an impact on the club's supporters than anything thrown at them over the past century.
Struggling AC Milan, in 12th place before Saturday's match, overcame Cup Winners' Cup hopefuls Fiorentina 2-0 to leapfrog them, Napoli and Lazio and move up to ninth.

French international midfielder Marcel Desailly headed in the first in the 61st minute from close range. Second half substitute Demetrio Albertini scored the second with an 89th minute penalty after George Weah was felled.
That result was revenge for Fiorentina's 2-1 victory in August in the Supercoppa, the traditional season opener between the league champions and domestic cup winners.
Many have seen Fiorentina's win then as the first real indication of once great Milan's decline and there were plenty of people ready to detect another turning point on Saturday.
